# Dialog

> A question or a short task that stops everything else until it's answered. A grey plate over the page with a title, a few words and its buttons.

## Install

It lands in `src/rost/dialog/`, with what it needs and its contract. In an app that uses shadcn:

```sh
npx shadcn add https://rost.build/r/dialog.json
```

Then import `src/rost/fonts.css` and `src/rost/tokens.css` once, at the root of the app. More on this in [Install](../INSTALL.md).

## Anatomy

- `root`: The browser's `<dialog>`, with its own look taken away. The browser shows and hides it, and centres it, so the plate is a part inside it.
- `panel`: The plate: the dialog's fill, a 1px edge and the floating shadow. It holds the title, the words and the buttons in a column, 16px apart.
- `title`: An `<h2>` in title type, medium weight.
- `body`: Paragraph type, a step quieter than the title.
- `actions`: The Buttons, in a row on the right, 8px apart. The main one goes last, where the eye ends up.

## When to use

- **Before something you can't undo.** Deleting an invoice, closing a year. Say what will happen in the title, and put it on the main button too.
- **A short task.** Two or three fields that belong to the screen behind, like renaming a client.

## When not to use

- **News.** Telling someone something happened. That's **Toast**: it doesn't stop them.
- **More detail.** Extra detail next to something. That's **Popover**, or **Disclosure** in the page.
- **Long forms.** Anything that scrolls. Give it a page.

## Behaviour

It opens as a modal: focus moves into it, the page behind can't be reached, and Esc closes it. That's the browser's `<dialog>` doing the work, not mine. The plate is Card's grey with an edge and the floating shadow. The dim layer behind it is still the browser's own: contracts don't have a way to style `::backdrop` yet, and I want that before I call this finished.

## Accessibility

- **Element**: `<dialog>` opened with `showModal()`, labelled by its title (`aria-labelledby`).
- **Name**: The title.
- **Keyboard**: Focus starts on the first thing you can press in it and stays inside until it closes. Esc closes it. Put the safe choice first, so a stray Enter doesn't delete anything.
- **Focus**: When it closes, focus goes back to what opened it. The browser does that too.
- **Colour**: The title is 14:1 and the words 11:1 on the plate, in dark.

## Content

The title asks the question ("Delete this invoice?"). The buttons answer it with verbs ("Keep it", "Delete"), never "Yes" and "No".
